title: Apply for a recreational fishing licence (3-day or 1-month)
summary: Find out about and apply for a short-term recreational fishing licence (3-day or 1-month) in NSW.
intro:
Recreational fishing licences are required in NSW, even if you only fish occasionally. Short-term (3-day or 1-month) and long-term (1-year or 3-year) licences are available.

Activities in NSW freshwater or saltwater that require a licence include:
who_can_apply: You need a licence if you are engaging in activities in NSW freshwater or saltwater that require a licence.
fees:
The NSW Government recreational fishing licence fees are:

You must show your licence fee receipt if asked by an authorised officer.

For more information on recreational fishing and licence fees visit NSW Primary Industries website.

### Fee exemptions

Not everyone has to pay a fee for a recreational fishing licence.

Check if you are eligible for a recreational fishing fee exemption.

If you are eligible, you'll need to carry the necessary proof with you when you're fishing, in case you're called upon to show it.

faqs.q: Do I need a fishing licence if I only fish occasionally?
faqs.a: Yes, recreational fishing licences are required in NSW, even if you only fish occasionally.

faqs.q: What types of fishing licences are available?
faqs.a: Short-term (3-day or 1-month) and long-term (1-year or 3-year) licences are available.

faqs.q: How do I apply for a licence?
faqs.a: You must select the 'Apply online' button, complete the online application form, provide a credit card, and show proof of identity.
